author: AnInstantNoodle
quote: GTA VI – A Step Backwards for the Franchise?It genuinely feels like GTA VI has had its roots neutered. Compared to previous entries in the franchise, the game feels noticeably dulled down, restricted and overly **** of the biggest things that made Grand Theft Auto what it was has always been the freedom to do whatever you wanted. That sense of unpredictability, unrestricted gameplay and being able to approach situations however you pleased. That freedom feels like it's slowly **** opening is an absolute slog. Instead of being thrown into the world and given the freedom to explore and play at your own pace, you're stuck doing what feels like an endless list of chores for Lucia. Fixing things around the house, running errands and carrying out mundane domestic tasks. It's an insufferable introduction that does very little to make you feel like you're actually playing a Grand Theft Auto **** this seems to be a wider issue throughout the game. There's an increasingly noticeable emphasis on domestic activities, relationship management and everyday responsibilities. At times, it feels less like GTA and more like a relationship simulator with a crime game bolted onto it.Rockstar seems to have confused realism with enjoyable gameplay. Having to manage increasingly mundane aspects of everyday life might make the world feel more realistic, but does it actually make the experience more entertaining? There's a point where immersion becomes busywork, and I feel GTA VI crosses that line far too often.What's more concerning is the apparent removal or restriction of mechanics that helped define previous titles. The freedom to interact with the world, engage in criminal activities and make your own decisions seems to have taken a back seat to Rockstar's increasingly controlled vision of how the game should be played. Even basic gameplay freedom feels compromised when so much seems dictated by story progression and predetermined activities.There's also a noticeable concern surrounding the game's identity. Where's the outrageous satire, the unapologetic dark humour and the ridiculous social commentary that made previous GTA games so entertaining? GTA was never supposed to be particularly tasteful or politically correct. Its willingness to push boundaries was part of its **** increasingly feels as though Rockstar is playing it safe, sanitising elements of the experience and restricting player interactions to avoid certain scenarios or controversies. An open-world crime game shouldn't feel like it's constantly putting boundaries around what you're allowed to do.There's a growing sense that the franchise is losing its rebellious edge. GTA used to thrive on letting players create absolute chaos, experiment with the world and do things simply because they could. Now, it feels as though Rockstar is more interested in controlling the experience than allowing players to enjoy it on their own terms.I appreciate the technical achievement, the attention to detail and the incredible world Rockstar has created. But impressive graphics, realistic animations and an incredibly detailed environment don't automatically translate into an enjoyable Grand Theft Auto experience. A beautiful open world means very little if the freedom to actually enjoy it has been stripped **** me, the biggest disappointment is that GTA VI seems to have lost sight of what made the franchise special in the first **** was about freedom, chaos, rebellion and doing things your own way. Not being micromanaged through a relationship, sent on domestic errands or restricted by an increasingly sanitised set of gameplay rules.Rockstar has created an impressive world, but I'm not convinced they've created a better Grand Theft Auto game.
